rows.citation: Tenn. Senate Permanent Rule of Order 71 (114th General Assembly)
rows.quote: The rules of parliamentary practice comprised in Mason's Manual of Legislative Procedure shall govern the Senate in all cases in which they are applicable, and in which they are not inconsistent with the foregoing rules.
rows.note: No explicit germaneness rule in the Senate Permanent Rules; Rule 24 repeats the one-subject/title requirement for bills. Requirement rests on Mason's sec. 402. Changes NCSL 2000 'no rule' entry to yes (Mason's).

rows.citation: Tenn. House Permanent Rule of Order 79 (114th General Assembly)
rows.quote: If any question shall arise which is not provided for in these rules, the same shall be governed by Mason's Manual of Legislative Procedure (latest edition existing on date of adoption of these rules), which is hereby adopted.
rows.note: No explicit germaneness rule in the House Permanent Rules (PDF is owner-password encrypted with an empty user password; decrypted locally for reading). Requirement rests on Mason's sec. 402. Changes NCSL 2000 'no rule' entry to yes (Mason's).

rows.citation: Tex. Const. art. III, sec. 30
rows.quote: no bill shall be so amended in its passage through either House, as to change its original purpose
rows.note: Constitutional 'original purpose'/'scope and object' test, binding on both chambers at every stage; narrower than a strict germaneness rule. NCSL (2000) also reported a chamber-rule germaneness provision (not reread).

rows.note: Constitutional 'original purpose'/'scope and object' test, binding on both chambers at every stage; narrower than a strict germaneness rule. NCSL (2000) also reported a chamber-rule germaneness provision (not reread).

rows.citation: Utah Senate Rule SR4-3-301(3) (floor amendments); SR4-3-202 (substitutes); SR3-2-406 (committee amendments)
rows.quote: The senator making the motion to amend shall ensure that the amendment is germane to the subject of the original legislation under consideration.
rows.note: A senator may raise a point of order and the presiding officer rules 'whether or not the amendment is germane to the subject of the original legislation.' Joint Rules rank Mason's Manual last among procedural sources.

rows.citation: Utah House Rule HR4-3-302 (floor amendments); HR4-3-202 (substitutes); HR3-2-406 (committee amendments)
rows.quote: The representative making the motion to amend shall ensure that the amendment is germane to the subject of the original legislation under consideration.
rows.note: Presiding officer rules on germaneness points of order. House rules permit Mason's Manual as a reference.

rows.citation: Vt. Senate Permanent Rule 91 (2025 edition)
rows.quote: Where a question of parliamentary procedure arises not covered by these Senate Rules, Mason's Manual of Legislative Procedure shall prevail, except Mason's Rule No. 780, as that rule is contrary to Senate procedures and customs.
rows.note: No explicit germaneness rule found in the Senate Permanent Rules (NCSL 2000 reported one); requirement now rests on Mason's sec. 402, which Rule 91 does not exclude.

rows.citation: Vt. House Rule 88 (Rules and Orders of the House, as amended 1/7/2026)
rows.quote: A question of parliamentary procedure not covered by these House Rules shall be decided according to Mason's Manual of Legislative Procedure.
rows.note: No explicit germaneness rule found in the House Rules text (NCSL 2000 reported one); requirement rests on Mason's sec. 402.

rows.citation: Va. Senate Rule 56 (Rules of the Senate, adopted 1/10/2024)
rows.quote: In the construction of the Rules, reference shall be had to the following sources in the following order: (a) Jefferson's Manual of Parliamentary Practice. (b) Mason's Manual of Legislative Procedure. (c) Standing Rules for Conducting Business in the Senate of the United States.
rows.note: Weak 'yes': the Senate rules (read) contain no rule requiring germane floor amendments ('germane' appears only in committee-referral provisions), and Rule 56 ranks Jefferson's Manual ahead of Mason's and places the U.S. Senate rules (which have no general germaneness rule) third. Jefferson's own amendment text was not read here. Treat as parliamentary-authority-derived only. Changes NCSL 2000 'no rule' entry to yes by the manual route. Route relabeled other-manual-adopted by the R6 session: the adopted authorities rank Jefferson's Manual first, so germaneness rests on inference (inferred).

rows.citation: Wash. Const. art. II, sec. 38
rows.quote: No amendment to any bill shall be allowed which shall change the scope and object of the bill.
rows.note: Constitutional 'original purpose'/'scope and object' test, binding on both chambers at every stage; narrower than a strict germaneness rule. NCSL (2000) also reported a chamber-rule germaneness provision (not reread).

rows.citation: Wash. Const. art. II, sec. 38
rows.quote: No amendment to any bill shall be allowed which shall change the scope and object of the bill.
rows.note: Constitutional 'original purpose'/'scope and object' test, binding on both chambers at every stage; narrower than a strict germaneness rule. NCSL (2000) also reported a chamber-rule germaneness provision (not reread).

rows.citation: W. Va. Senate Rules, 'Parliamentary Procedure' (final rule)
rows.quote: In all cases not provided for by the Rules of the Senate or any adopted Joint Rules of the Senate and House of Delegates, the Senate shall be governed by Jefferson's Manual and Rules of the House of Representatives of the United States Congress and practices thereunder.
rows.note: Senate rules (read) contain no explicit germaneness rule. The adopted fallback is Jefferson's Manual plus the U.S. House rules, whose Rule XVI cl. 7 bars a 'motion or proposition on a subject different from that under consideration' under color of amendment (U.S. House rule not refetched here). Changes NCSL 2000 'no rule' entry to yes by the adopted-authority route; weaker than a Senate rule. Route relabeled other-manual-adopted by the R6 session: the adopted authorities rank Jefferson's Manual first, so germaneness rests on inference (inferred).

rows.citation: W. Va. House Rule 113; see also Rule 62
rows.quote: No amendment shall be in order that is not germane to the matter under consideration; and the Speaker, when the question is raised, shall rule as to the admissibility of the proposed amendment.
rows.note: Rule 62 ('Motion Must Be Germane'): 'No motion on a subject different from that under consideration shall be admitted under color of amendment.' Rule 135 (2023) makes Mason's Manual, 2020 edition, the parliamentary authority after the state constitution.

rows.citation: Wis. Senate Rule 50 (Senate Rules as last affected by 2023 Senate Resolution 2)
rows.quote: Every substitute amendment and amendment to a proposal must be germane to that proposal.
rows.note: Rule 50 lists amendments that are and are not germane (for example, one that substantially expands the scope or negates the proposal is not germane). The presiding officer rules on germaneness.

rows.citation: Wis. Assembly Rule 54(1) (Assembly Rules as last affected by 2025 Assembly Resolution 2)
rows.quote: The assembly may not consider any assembly amendment or assembly substitute amendment that relates to a different subject or is intended to accomplish a different purpose than that of the proposal
rows.note: Rule 54 continues with a relating-clause test and a list of germane and non-germane amendments; the question is not in order once the amendment is adopted. Assembly Rule 8 references Jefferson's Manual for committee of the whole.

rows.citation: Wyo. Const. art. 3, sec. 20
rows.quote: no bill shall be so altered or amended on its passage through either house as to change its original purpose
rows.note: Constitutional 'original purpose'/'scope and object' test, binding on both chambers at every stage; narrower than a strict germaneness rule. NCSL (2000) listed this chamber as having no germaneness provision in its own rules, so the constraint here is constitutional only.

rows.citation: Wyo. Const. art. 3, sec. 20

rows.chamberName: Council of the District of Columbia
rows.citation: Rules of Organization and Procedure for the Council, Council Period 26, Rule 356; Rule 1001 adopts Mason's
rows.quote: Amendments to a bill or resolution shall be germane to the subject matter of the measure or to the section or title thereof to which the amendment is proposed.
rows.note: Rule number came from a summarizing fetch of the enrolled rules; confirm. Mason's Manual governs where the rules are silent.

rows.citation: P.R. Const. art. III, sec. 17
rows.quote: No bill shall be amended in a manner that changes its original purpose or incorporates matters extraneous to it.
rows.note: English text read from an unofficial transcription; official Spanish text not checked. Covers both original purpose and 'extraneous' matter. NCSL (2000): neither chamber returned survey.

rows.citation: Standing Rules of the 33rd Guam Legislature (2015), Rule VI, sec. 6.01(a); Rule V, sec. 5.01 adopts Mason's (2010 ed.)

rows.citation: CNMI Senate Interim Rules of Procedure, 24th Legislature (adopted 1/13/2025), Rule 18
rows.quote: If any ambiguity or conflict should arise regarding these Rules, or if these Rules do not address a question or situation that may arise, then such controversy shall first be resolved according to the rules and principles outlined in Mason's Manual of Legislative Procedure, 2020 Edition (Mason's Manual).
rows.note: Senate rules (read) have no explicit germaneness rule for amendments; Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised is the second fallback. The rules are titled 'Interim' Rules. CNMI Const. art. II, sec. 5 has no original-purpose clause.

rows.chamberName: Northern Mariana Islands House of Representatives
rows.citation: CNMI House Rules of Procedure, 24th Legislature (adopted 1/13/2025), Rule IX, sec. 12
rows.quote: Amendments to bills or resolutions may be offered on the Floor by any member; provided, that the proposed amendment is in writing and is germane to the measure.
rows.note: Rule XVI, sec. 2 makes Mason's Manual the first fallback authority and Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised the second. CNMI Const. art. II, sec. 5 (read at https://cnmilaw.gov/constitution) has a one-subject rule but no amendment/original-purpose clause.

rows.citation: House Rule XVI, clause 7
rows.quote: No motion or proposition on a subject different from that under consideration shall be admitted under color of amendment.
rows.note: Tests in House Practice ch. 26: subject matter, fundamental purpose, committee jurisdiction, method, and general vs. specific. Often waived or shaped by special rules from the Rules Committee.

rows.citation: Riddick's Senate Procedure, 'Germaneness of Amendments'; Senate Rules XXII (cloture) and XVI (general appropriations)
rows.quote: The Senate does not have a general rule requiring that amendments be germane to the measure to which they are proposed.
rows.note: Stage-limited: germaneness is required after cloture (Rule XXII), on general appropriation bills (Rule XVI, question decided by Senate vote), under the Budget Act for budget and reconciliation measures, and often by unanimous-consent agreements.
